Energetics

Oxidation of palmitic acid: 7 turns of β-oxidation (7 FADH₂ and 7 NADH — by the textbook, 7 × 5 = 35 ATP) and 8 acetyl-CoA (8 × 12 = 96 ATP), minus 2 ATP for activation (ATP → AMP) — about 129 ATP (≈ 106 with modern coefficients). Glycerol gives another ~22 ATP. Per gram, fat stores more than twice as much energy as carbohydrate.

Ketone bodies

Synthesis: 2 acetyl-CoA → acetoacetyl-CoA → HMG-CoA → acetoacetate → β-hydroxybutyrate (by reduction) or acetone (spontaneously). Use in tissues: acetoacetate + succinyl-CoA → acetoacetyl-CoA → 2 acetyl-CoA → Krebs cycle. The liver lacks the necessary enzyme (succinyl-CoA:3-ketoacid CoA transferase, or thiophorase), so it only exports ketones.

Disorders

Carnitine deficiency (in premature infants, on hemodialysis) — muscle weakness, hypoglycemia. Inherited defects of acyl-CoA dehydrogenases. Obesity — lipogenesis outweighing lipolysis.
